doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

title: His wife pushes him to write the three movements; melodic taste and heroes
summary: The slow movement began as a sample for a book; his wife told him to write the first and third. He prefers melodic music and names Rachmaninoff, Debussy, Ravel, Satie and Chopin.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’m going to tell you something. The first one I recorded with the London Symphony in Abbey Road Studio years ago. And the first one I wrote a little piece for one of my book, it’s supposed to be like a second movement, like a slow movement of a theme, as a sample, and I included it in the book. And I was doing a recording of that at home and my wife asked me, “What is that?” And I explained to her and she said, “Okay. Now start writing the first and the third.” I said, “What!” “Yeah. Now — you have the second already. Go ahead and write the first and the third.” I said, “Oh come on.” She said, “Yes, do it.” My wife, you know we call her the “Big Boss.” We are married for 48 years you know.
And then I said, “Okay, I’m going to try.” I did it and then I recorded it. And with the second one it was exactly the same thing.
Did you start with the second movement?

Yes I wrote a piece and then I recorded it here at home you know and she said, “Wow, that sounds like a second movement of a concerto. Okay. You know what you have to do, I don’t have to tell you again.” The second one is more simple to be honest. It’s more melodic. It’s not very technical and it’s not very complicated at all. Because to be honest, I’m not a big fan of those kind of trumpet concertos, the modern music that has no melodies [scats]. I say wow, I cannot repeat that in my dreams, or I cannot memorize those melodies and harmonies and themes, because I love very much melodic music. My favorite composer is Sergei Rachmaninoff. You know. And then I’m crazy about Debussy and Ravel and Satie, and those people who write — Chopin — all those people who write beautiful, beautiful melodies. They are my heroes you know. And that’s what I’m trying to do in almost all my compositions you know. I’m trying to be melodic and kind of — it’s always a little bit of romanticism involved in what I do.
